goal: Adds wallet support for receiving BIP-352 Silent Payments: a new sp() descriptor, scanning logic, and change-address selection so wallets can generate and detect silent payment outputs.
Solves the lack of first-party silent payment support in Bitcoin Core, letting users receive with a single reusable address without leaking it on-chain.
reviewability: Not reviewable right now: marked Needs rebase, based on two still-open prerequisite PRs (#35301, #35302), and blocked externally on an unresolved libsecp256k1 issue before the new crypto module can ship in a release.
A material test-review comment from rkrux (2026-06-27) has gone unanswered for well over a week.
agreement: Sustained, substantive multi-year review from josibake and Sjors with concrete design pushback (scan-key modeling, fast-rescan behavior, change-address logic) that the author iteratively addressed (Eunovo).
Bug reports from macgyver13 during backup/restore testing were fixed and confirmed working (macgyver13).
No unresolved blocking objections, but scope was narrowed with labels functionality explicitly deferred to a follow-up (josibake, Eunovo).
Latest partial review from rkrux (2026-06-27) raised only nits, pending the stacked PRs landing first.

result.summary: This PR implements the receiving side of BIP-352 Silent Payments for the Bitcoin Core wallet: a new sp() descriptor type, a SilentPaymentsDescriptorScriptPubKeyMan that scans blocks for silent payment outputs, wallet/GUI options to create silent-payments wallets, and logic to prefer silent-payment change addresses when spending to silent-payment or taproot destinations. It also vendors a new silentpayments module into the libsecp256k1 subtree and adds BIP-352 primitives, tests, and functional tests. Labels support is explicitly incomplete and deferred to a follow-up PR.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core wallet users currently have no first-party way to receive payments to a reusable address without exposing linkage on-chain; Silent Payments (BIP-352) solves this, and this PR is the receiving half of that long-tracked project (issue #28536).

open_concerns: A material test-review comment from rkrux (2026-06-27, hardcoded descriptor checksum, duplicate helper function) is unanswered.
Whether the silent-payments wallet flag should be mutable via setwalletflag or auto-set on descriptor import remains undecided (Sjors, Eunovo, no final resolution).
Labels functionality is intentionally incomplete, deferred to a follow-up PR (josibake, Eunovo).
resolved_concerns: Design disagreement over modeling the scan key as a CKey vs a custom type was resolved by introducing ScankeyPubkeyProvider/SpDescriptor, which josibake confirmed simplified the code substantially.
Multiple import/backup/restore bugs found by macgyver13 (import warnings, missing SP addresses after import) were fixed and confirmed resolved.
Fast-rescan behavior for silent-payments wallets was clarified and documented as an intentional limitation (josibake, Eunovo, Sjors).

result.card: This draft PR implements the receiving side of BIP-352 Silent Payments for Bitcoin Core: a new sp() descriptor, a scanning ScriptPubKeyMan, silent-payment-aware change selection, and a vendored libsecp256k1 silentpayments module with BIP-352 test vectors. It solves the lack of native support for a privacy-preserving reusable payment address, a feature many users and the project's own long-running Silent Payments tracking issue (#28536) have wanted. Review has been substantive and largely positive for 15+ months (josibake, Sjors, macgyver13 testing backup/restore and fixing real bugs), with labels support explicitly deferred to a follow-up. It is currently Stale: marked Needs rebase, stacked on two still-open prerequisite PRs (#35301, #35302), and the author says the real blocker is an unresolved upstream libsecp256k1 issue before the new crypto primitives can ship in a release.
